raw_case_text:
A 35-year-old male presented with recurrent episodes of high grade fever without diurnal variation with red, raised lesions for past 1 year. The lesions were mainly present on face, ears, upper trunk, and upper limbs and the present episode was for 1 week. He had had six such episodes in the past 1 year. He also complained of pain in bilateral knee joints for 1 week without any swelling or restricted movements.
Patient was on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for past 1 year with zidovudine, lamivudine, and efavirenz. He had inguinal lymphadenitis 7 months ago for which fine needle aspiration cytology was done which showed tubercular lymphadenitis, and antitubercular treatment (ATT) was instituted. He is now taking isoniazid 300 mg, rifampicin 450 mg, and ethambutol 825 mg. He had taken MDT twice in the past year for multibacillary leprosy and was a defaulter. On examination, patient was febrile on presentation and emaciated with body mass inde x18.5 kg/m2. Severe pallor with bilateral pitting pedal edema was noted. There was glove and stocking anesthesia on bilateral hands and feet with thickening of right superficial radial, bilateral ulnar, and common peroneal nerve. Patient had tender erythematous nodules on his face, upper limbs, upper trunk, and ears [Figures 1 and 2]. There was no associated nerve tenderness, testicular swelling, lymphadenopathy, ocular pain, or photophobia. His investigations showed severe anemia with hemoglobin (Hb) 4.4 g% and mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 77 fl, and total count was 3,700 cells/mm3, but his differential count was normal. Absolute CD4 lymphocyte count was 90 cells/mul and dipstick enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for filarial antigen was positive. His liver and renal function tests, chest X-ray, X-ray of bilateral knee joints, and urine routine were within normal limits. Blood and stool culture and streptococcal throat swab showed no growth of organisms and his Widal test for typhoid and microscopy for malarial parasite was negative. Skin-slit smear was 6+ for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) [Figure 3]. Biopsy from a nodule showed superficial and deep periadnexal granulomatous inflammation with neutrophils and nuclear debris around vessels [Figure 4]. Lepra stain showed fragmented AFB. Based on the above, a diagnosis of AIDS, lepromatous leprosy with type 2 lepra reaction manifesting as ENL, tubercular lymphadenitis, and filariasis was made. The patient was started on clofazimine 50 mg daily and monthly 300 mg supervised dose, rifampicin 150 mg monthly, ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily, thalidomide 100 mg daily, and diethylcarbamazine 100 mg thrice daily with iron supplements. Dapsone was stopped due to fear of further hemolysis and zidovudine was stopped for suspicion of bone marrow suppression. The patient improved dramatically and his lesions resolved within 1 week. The patient is on our follow-up and free from any reaction.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old male presented with a 1-year history of recurrent high-grade fever and erythematous raised skin lesions (current flare of 1 week's duration) accompanied by bilateral knee joint pain for 1 week.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced six episodes of high-grade fever without diurnal variation accompanied by red, raised skin lesions over the face, ears, upper trunk, and upper limbs over the past year, with the current episode lasting 1 week. He also reported a 1-week history of bilateral knee joint pain without joint swelling or restricted range of motion.
subjective.past_medical_history: Known HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, efavirenz) for the past 1 year. Diagnosed with tuberculous inguinal lymphadenitis via fine-needle aspiration cytology 7 months prior and currently on antitubercular therapy (isoniazid 300 mg, rifampicin 450 mg, ethambutol 825 mg). History of multibacillary leprosy for which he took multidrug therapy (MDT) twice in the past year and defaulted.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent high-grade fever, painful erythematous skin nodules, and bilateral knee arthralgia. Pertinent negatives: no joint swelling or restricted movement, no nerve pain, no testicular swelling, no ocular pain, and no photophobia. Home medications: zidovudine, lamivudine, efavirenz, isoniazid 300 mg, rifampicin 450 mg, ethambutol 825 mg, and dapsone.

objective.physical_examination: On presentation, the patient was febrile and emaciated (BMI 18.5 kg/m^2) with severe pallor and bilateral pitting pedal edema. Cutaneous examination revealed tender erythematous nodules over the face, ears, upper trunk, and upper limbs. Neurological examination demonstrated bilateral glove-and-stocking anesthesia over the hands and feet, with palpable thickening of the right superficial radial nerve, bilateral ulnar nerves, and common peroneal nerves, without nerve tenderness. There was no lymphadenopathy or testicular swelling.
objective.routine_investigations: Severe microcytic anemia with hemoglobin 4.4 g% and MCV 77 fL; total leukocyte count 3,700 cells/mm^3 with a normal differential count; absolute CD4 lymphocyte count 90 cells/µL. Dipstick ELISA for filarial antigen was positive. Liver and renal function tests, routine urinalysis, chest X-ray, and bilateral knee radiographs were normal. Blood culture, stool culture, streptococcal throat swab, Widal test for typhoid, and peripheral blood microscopy for malarial parasites were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Slit-skin smear was 6+ for acid-fast bacilli (AFB). Skin punch biopsy from an erythematous nodule demonstrated superficial and deep periadnexal granulomatous inflammation with neutrophils and perivascular nuclear debris (leukocytoclastic vasculitis), and Lepra stain showed fragmented acid-fast bacilli.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) complicated by lepromatous leprosy in type 2 lepra reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum, ENL), tuberculous inguinal lymphadenitis, and lymphatic filariasis, confirmed by slit-skin smear (6+ AFB), skin biopsy with Lepra stain, CD4 count (90 cells/µL), and positive filarial antigen ELISA. Typhoid fever (Widal, blood/stool cultures), malaria, and streptococcal infection were ruled out. Dapsone was discontinued due to concern for hemolysis and zidovudine was stopped for suspected bone marrow suppression. Treatment was initiated with clofazimine (50 mg daily plus 300 mg monthly supervised), rifampicin (150 mg monthly), ofloxacin (200 mg twice daily), thalidomide (100 mg daily), diethylcarbamazine (100 mg three times daily), and iron supplementation. His skin lesions and fever resolved dramatically within 1 week, and he remained reaction-free on follow-up.
